passages.original: Videtur repugnare Cornelii testimonium, qui Nova- tianum in persecutione Decii fratribus auxilio indi- gentibus succurrere noluisse testatur apud Euse- bium (15). Sed forte haec humanitatis existimatio ad Novatianum pervenit ex praeclarissimis cleri Romani litteris inter Cyprianicas XXXI, quae a No- vatiano scriptae in totum orbem missae fuerunt, teste Cypriano epistola 1 et 2. Verum de hoc vide quae alibi disseruimus, ubi de Novatiani epistola Romani cleri nomine scripta, verba fecimus (16).
passages.english: The testimony of Cornelius seems to conflict [with this], for he attests, as reported by Eusebius (15), that Novatian in the persecution of Decius refused to help brethren in need of assistance. But perhaps this reputation for humanity came to Novatian from the most illustrious letter of the Roman clergy, number XXXI among the Cyprianic [letters], which was written by Novatian and sent out to the whole world, as Cyprian testifies in epistles 1 and 2. But on this see what we have discussed elsewhere, where we spoke about Novatian's letter written in the name of the Roman clergy (16).
passages.notes: The numbers (15) and (16) are the edition's footnote references, kept as in the text. The phrase "epistola 1 et 2" is unclear. It may refer to particular letters of Cyprian under some edition's numbering, or to two passages in one letter.
